messages:
jordan: Thinking out loud — we need a concrete delivery pattern for change-evidence (who/what/when) in the console. Two options on the table: presigned bundle downloads (NDJSON ZIP) vs live streaming webhooks/NDJSON to SIEMs. Also need to decide telemetry hooks for quota + rollout metrics. where do people stand?

maria: +1 need to pick one default UX. presigned feels safest for legal requests (immutable snapshot) but streaming is nicer for realtime monitoring. :thinking_face:

kevin: presigned wins for auditability. easier to attach signature, retention, and retention TTL. streaming needs guaranteed delivery + deduping logic on our side or consumer side.

elaine: +1 on presigned for downloads, but can we offer streaming as an opt-in push with backpressure? e.g., short-lived websocket + sliding window, not raw firehose.

jordan: agreed. two-tier offering maybe: canonical snapshot download for compliance + lightweight telemetry stream (sampling) for dashboards and rollouts UX? main question: how to surface "who changed what" in the snapshot vs the streamed events so consumers don't have to join them later.

kevin: minimal schema proposal: each exported event should include actor_id, actor_display (if available), tenant_id, entity_path, before/after diff (or pointer to object snapshot), change_ts, change_id. For presigned bundles we include a manifest.json with bundle-level meta + signed hash. For stream we emit same event shape, but indicate "stream": true.

maria: can we avoid putting PII like actor email in the export by default? redwood prefers pseudonymization. maybe include actor_hint (short name) and actor_id, then a per-tenant opt-in for full actor metadata.

elaine: yes — privacy flagging should be top-level. Also need UI copy: "Download compliance snapshot (contains actor IDs; full actor info depends on tenant settings)". Legal will want clarity.

jordan: telemetry + quotas: we need to charge/download quotas for snapshot exports (they can be expensive). For streaming telemetry we could sample 1% by default and provide quota-free small streams for tenants with premium flag. Thoughts?

kevin: charging snapshots as heavy-weight operations makes sense; enforce rate limit like 1 snapshot per 24h per tenant by default, with overrides via dedicated/reserved capacity. For stream sampling: sample rate config per-tenant + server-side sampling keys to ensure determinism.

maria: UX question: when a tenant requests a snapshot during a rollout (canary->prod), do we include rollout metadata (which version served request, routing policy) inline? customers will expect mapping between a change event and the rollout that produced behavioral differences.

elaine: include rollout_id and model/version metadata if available. Might be null for older events. Also include route_policy_id. We should avoid inflating payloads — provide pointers (IDs) and a companion small lookup file in the bundle with human-friendly strings.

kevin: implementation note: presigned bundles should be signed with our export signing key; include a verification endpoint (/exports/verify?bundle_hash=...) and a signed merkle-ish manifest so security teams can validate integrity.

ops-bot: deploy svc/export-worker v1.3.1 -> prod finished (abc123) :white_check_mark:

jordan: nice. API debate: should we surface this via a single /v1/exports endpoint with params {mode: "snapshot"|"stream", scope: "tenant"|"route"|"time-window", include_actor_meta: bool, sample_rate: float} OR separate endpoints /v1/snapshots and /v1/streams?

maria: single endpoint with mode param is simpler for SDKs. separate endpoints might be clearer for internal ops and RBAC.

kevin: I'm leaning single endpoint but different response shapes. enforce RBAC checks server-side (snapshots require export:read, streams require telemetry:subscribe).

elaine: agree single endpoint. For console UX we can show two CTA buttons that call the same API with different params. Keep console flow simple: "Download snapshot" and "Open telemetry stream".

jordan: rollout UX: when snapshot is triggered, capture the active routing policy and include a small "policy_snapshot.json" in the bundle. That will make diffs easier for support triage. Also record a telemetry event for quota billing (export_request.{accepted,rejected,delivered}).

maria: we should also emit a background 1-off attribution trace that links change_ids to trace_ids for 72h retention to help root-cause analyses. Keep it short-lived.

kevin: agreed. operational concern: large snapshots could be heavy on compactor nodes. Suggest we stream generation to S3 and provide progress events. UI shows progress and estimated size. If bundle > X GB require a confirmed second-factor click.

elaine: UX microcopy: when large snapshot is requested show: "This export may contain sensitive actor identifiers and could take up to 45 minutes. Confirm to continue."

jordan: follow-ups: 1) schema doc PR from @kevin by EOD Friday 2) RBAC gating matrix from @maria 3) console mockups + progress UX from @elaine. I'll draft export signing proposal for security.

maria: ACK, will add quota table to the PR.

kevin: will do schema and example ndjson to the spec repo.

elaine: mockups scheduled for Wed design review.

jordan: thanks all. tagging legal and security offline. :thumbsup:

maria: :eyes: also pinging support for expected customer asks.
